children: An additional rise in the Reserve Bank of Australia's official cash rate to 4.85%, from 4.60%, on Tuesday will put interest rates at their highest level in 18 years. The increase is nearly 90% expected by financial markets after recent poor inflation data and pretty clear messaging from the bank's senior management. The RBA is facing a major challenge as risks grow of a recession in the economy next year with policy makers trying to bring inflation back down to target. The bank has been clear about the hard choices it faces and increasingly it appears as though the fallout for the economy could be dramatic. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
